div.head: TOM BULLOCK
div.p: TO THOSE WHO ENJOY SNUG CLUB ROOMS, THAT THEY MAY LEARN THE ART OF PREPARING FOR THEMSELVES WHAT IS GOOD.

IS IT ANY WONDER THAT MANKIND STANDS OPEN-MOUTHED BEFORE THE BARTENDER, CONSIDERING THE MYSTERIES AND MARVELS OF AN ART THAT BORDERS ON MAGIC? RECIPES FOUND IN THIS BOOK HAVE BEEN COMPOSED AND COLLECTED, TRIED AND TESTED, IN A QUARTER-CENTURY OF EXPERIENCE BY TOM BULLOCK OF THE ST. LOUIS COUNTRY CLUB.

A testimonial from the St. Louis Post-Dispatch which appeared in the form of an editorial, Wednesday evening, May 28, 1913, at a time when Col. Roosevelt was vindicating, by a libel suit, his reputation for sobriety and temperance.
Colonel Roosevelt's fatal admission that he drank just a part of one julep at the St. Louis Country Club will come very near losing his case.

Who was ever known to drink just a part of one of Tom's? Tom, than whom there is no greater mixologist of any race, color or condition of servitude, was taught the art of the julep by no less than Marse Lilburn G. McNair, the father of the julep. In fact, the very cup that Col. Roosevelt drank it from belonged to Governor McNair, the first Governor of Missouri, the great-grandfather of Marse Lilburn and the great-great-grandfather of the julep.

As is well known, the Country Club mint originally sprang on the slopes of Parnassus and was transplanted thence to the bosky banks of Culpeper Creek, Gaines County, Ky., and thence to our own environs; while the classic distillation with which Tom mingles it to produce his chief d'oeuvre is the oft-quoted liquefied soul of a Southern moonbeam falling aslant the dewy slopes of the Cumberland Mountains.

To believe that a red-blooded man, and a true Colonel at that, ever stopped with just a part of one of those refreshments which have made St. Louis hospitality proverbial and become one of our most distinctive genre institutions, is to strain credulity too far. Are the Colonel's powers of self restraint altogether transcendent? Have we found the living superman at last?
When the Colonel says that he consumed just a part of one he doubtless meant that he did not swallow the Mint itself, munch the ice and devour the very cup.

div.head: INTRODUCTION
div.p: I have known the author of "The Ideal Bartender" for many years, and it is a genuine privilege to be permitted to testify to his qualifications for such a work.

To his many friends in St. Louis, Louisville, Cincinnati, Chicago and elsewhere, my word will be superfluous, but to those who do not know him, and who are to be the gainers by following his advices, it may prove at the very beginning a stimulus to know something of his record of achievement.

For the past quarter of a century he has refreshed and delighted the members and their friends of the Pendennis Club of Louisville and the St. Louis Country Club of St. Louis. In all that time I doubt if he has erred in even one of his concoctions. Thus if there is "many a slip twixt the cup and the lip" it has been none of his doing, but rather the fault of those who have appreciated his art too highly. But why go on! His work is before you. It is the best to be had. Follow on, and as you sip the nectar of his schemings tell your friends, to the end that both they and he may be benefitted.

div.head: ABRICONTINE POUSSE CAFE
div.p: Fill Pousse Cafe glass one-third full of Abricontine and add Maraschino, Curacoa, Chartreuse and Brandy in equal proportions until the glass is filled. The ingredients should be poured in one after the other from a small Wine glass, with great care, to prevent the colors from blending. Ignite the Brandy on top, and after it has blazed for a few seconds extinguishing it by placing a saucer or the bottom of another glass over the blazing fluid. Then serve.

div.head: ABSINTHE
div.p: (When the customer asks for Absinthe without specifying any particular style of service).

Pour one pony of Absinthe into large Bar glass and let ice cold water drip from the Absinthe glass into Bar glass until full. The Absinthe glass has a hole in the center. By filling the bowl of the Absinthe glass partly with Shaved Ice, and the rest with water, the water will be ice cold as it drops from the Absinthe glass.

div.head: ABSINTHE, AMERICAN SERVICE
div.p: Mixing glass ¾ full Shaved Ice.
Shake until outside of shaker is well frosted; strain into large Champagne glass and serve.

div.head: ABSINTHE COCKTAIL
div.p: Mixing glass ¾ full Shaved Ice.
Stir; strain into Cocktail glass and serve.

div.head: ABSINTHE FRAPPE
div.p: Fill medium Bar glass full of Shaved Ice.
Shake until outside of Shaker has frosty appearance; strain into six-ounce Shell glass and serve.

div.head: ABSINTHE, FRENCH SERVICE
div.p: Pour 1 pony of Absinthe into a Champagne glass which is standing in a bowl. Fill the bowl of your Absinthe glass with Shaved Ice and water. Raise the bowl and let the Ice Water drip into the Absinthe until the proper color is obtained. Serve in thin Bar glass.

div.head: ABSINTHE, ITALIAN SERVICE
div.p: 1 pony of Absinthe in a large Bar glass.
Pour Ice Water in glass, at same time stirring gently with Bar Spoon. Serve.

div.head: ADMIRAL SCHLEY HIGH BALL
div.p: Drop a piece of Ice into a High Ball glass.
⅔ jigger Tokay, Angelica or Sweet Catawba Wine.
Fill up with Apollinaris or Seltzer.

div.head: ALE FLIP
div.p: Fill an Ale glass nearly full.
Break in 1 whole Egg; grate a little Nutmeg on top and serve the drink with a spoon alongside of the glass.

div.head: ALE SANGAREE
div.p: Dissolve in an Ale glass 1 teaspoonful Bar Sugar. Fill up with Ale and serve with grated Nutmeg on top.

div.head: AMERICAN POUSSE CAFE
div.p: Fill a Pousse Cafe glass ¼ full of Chartreuse, and add Maraschino, Curacoa and Brandy in equal proportions until the glass is filled. Then proceed as for Abricontine Pousse Cafe.

div.head: APOLLINARIS LEMONADE
div.p: Fill large Bar glass ⅔ full Shaved Ice.
Fill up with Apollinaris; stir; strain into Lemonade glass dress with Fruit and serve.

div.head: APPLE JACK COCKTAIL
div.p: Fill large Bar glass ¾ full Shaved Ice.
Shake; strain into Cocktail glass and serve with piece of Lemon Peel twisted on top.

div.head: APPLEJACK FIX
div.p: Fill large Bar glass with Shaved Ice.
2 teaspoonfuls Bar Sugar, dissolved in little Water.
Stir; dress with Fruits; serve with Straws.

div.head: APPLEJACK SOUR
div.p: Fill large Bar glass ¾ full Shaved Ice.
2 teaspoonfuls Bar Sugar, dissolved in little Water.
Stir well; strain into Sour glass; dress with Fruit and Berries and serve.

div.head: "ARF-AND-ARF"
div.p: Pour into an Ale glass or mug ½ Porter and ½ Ale, or Porter and Stout with Ale, or ½ Old and ½ New Ale.
The use of the Porter and Ale is more prevalent in England. In the United States ½ Old and ½ New Ale is usually used when this drink is called for, unless otherwise specified.

div.head: ARRACK PUNCH
div.p: Pour into a Punch glass the Juice of 1 Lime and a little Apollinaris Water in which a heaping teaspoonful of Bar Sugar has been dissolved. Add:
Stir well; dash with Champagne; stir again briskly; dress with Fruit and Serve.

div.head: ASTRINGENT
div.p: Fill up with Brandy; stir gently and serve with little Nutmeg on top.

div.head: AUDITORIUM COOLER
div.p: Into large Bar glass squeeze Juice of 1 Lemon.
1 bottle Ginger Ale off the ice.
Stir; decorate with Fruit and Berries, Serve.

div.head: ALL RIGHT COCKTAIL
div.p: Use a large Mixing glass filled with Lump Ice.
Shake well; strain into Cocktail glass and serve.

div.head: BACARDI COCKTAIL
div.p: Shake well and serve in a Cocktail glass.

div.head: BACARDI COCKTAIL—Country Club Style
div.p: Shake well; strain into Cocktail glass and serve.

div.head: BALDY COCKTAIL
div.p: Use a large Mixing glass with Lump Ice.
1 jigger of Burnette's Old Tom Gin.
Shake; strain into Cocktail glass and serve.

div.head: BAMBOO COCKTAIL
div.p: Fill large Bar glass ⅓ full Fine Ice.
Stir; strain into Cocktail glass. Serve.

div.head: BLACK COW
div.p: Use a large Mixing glass with Lump Ice.
Stir well and serve with Straws.

div.head: BLOOD HOUND COCKTAIL
div.p: Fill large Bar glass ½ full Shaved Ice.
Shake well; strain into Cocktail glass and serve.

div.head: BOMBAY COCKTAIL
div.p: Break one Ice Cold Egg into glass.
Add salt and Spanish Paprica and serve.

div.head: BENEDICTINE
div.p: Place an inverted Whiskey glass on the bar, set a Pony glass on it and fill up with Benedictine. Serve all liquors straight in this manner.

div.head: BEEF TEA
div.p: ½ teaspoonful Beef Extract in small Bar glass.
Fill glass with Hot Water. Stir well while seasoning with Pepper, Salt and Celery Salt. Serve with small glass of Cracked Ice and spoon on the side.

div.head: BISHOP
div.p: 1 teaspoonful Bar Sugar in large Bar glass.
2 dashes Lemon Juice with the Skin of Two Slices.
Fill glass ¾ full Shaved Ice.
Fill up with Claret or Burgundy; shake; ornament with Fruit and serve with Straws.

div.head: BISHOP A LA PRUSSE
div.p: Before a Fire or in a Hot Oven roast 6 large Oranges until they are of a light brown color, and then place them in a deep dish and scatter over them ½ lb. of Granulated Sugar and pour on 1 pint of Port or Claret Wine. Then cover the dish and set aside for 24 hours before the time to serve. When about ready for the service, set the dish in boiling water; press the Juice from the Oranges with a large spoon or wooden potato masher and strain the Juice through a fine seive or cheese cloth. Then boil 1 pint of Port or Claret and mix it with the Strained Juice. Serve in stem Claret glasses while warm. A little Nutmeg on top improves the drink, but should not be added unless requested by customer or guest.

div.head: BISMARCK
div.p: 2 teaspoonfuls Vanilla Cordial in Sherry Wine glass.
1 yolk of an Egg covered with Benedictine so as not to break the yolk.
The colors should be kept separate and great care exercised to prevent the ingredients from running together.

div.head: BIZZY IZZY HIGH BALL
div.p: Drop 1 piece of Ice into a Highball glass.
½ jigger Rye or Bourbon Whiskey.

div.head: BLACK STRIPE
div.p: Pour Wineglass Santa Cruz or Jamaica Rum into a small Bar glass and add 1 tablespoonful of Molasses.
If to serve hot, fill glass with boiling Water and sprinkle Nutmeg on top.
If to serve cold, add ½ Wineglass Water. Stir well and fill up with Shaved Ice.

div.head: BLACK AND TAN PUNCH (For party of 10)
div.p: Pour into mixture of Lemon Juice and Sugar the Champagne and Stout, ice cold. Serve in Punch glasses dressed with Fruit.

div.head: BLACKTHORNE COCKTAIL
div.p: Fill Mixing glass ⅔ full Shaved Ice.
Stir; strain into Cocktail glass and serve.

div.head: BLACKTHORNE SOUR
div.p: Fill large Bar glass ⅔ full Shaved Ice.
Stir; strain into Claret glass; ornament with Fruit and serve.

div.head: BLIZ'S ROYAL RICKEY
div.p: Drop 3 lumps Cracked Ice in a Rickey (thin Champagne) glass.
Fill up with Ginger Ale (imported); stir; dress with Fruit and serve.

div.head: BLUE BLAZER
div.p: Use two Pewter or Silver Mugs.
1 teaspoonful Bar Sugar dissolved in a little Hot Water.
Ignite the mixture, and while blazing pour it several times from one mug to the other. Serve with a piece of twisted Lemon Peel on top.

div.head: BOATING PUNCH
div.p: Into a large Bar glass put:
Fill up with Shaved Ice and add:
Stir; dress with Fruit and serve with Straws.

div.head: BOMBAY PUNCH (2½-gallon mixture for 40 people)
div.p: Bruise the skins of 6 Lemons in 1 lb. of Bar sugar and put the Sugar in a Punch bowl and add:
Stir well; empty into another bowl in which a block of Clear Ice has been placed and add:
Serve into Punch glasses so that each person will have some of the Fruit.

div.head: BON SOIR ("Good Night")
div.p: Fill a Sherry glass ½ full of Shaved Ice.
Fill up with Ginger Ale; stir gently and serve with a Straw cut in two.

div.head: BOSTON COOLER
div.p: 1 Lemon Rind in large Bar glass. 3 lumps Ice. 1 bottle Ginger Ale. 1 bottle Sarsaparilla.

div.head: BOTTLE OF COCKTAIL
div.p: Pour a quart of Whiskey or other Liquor desired into a Bar measure or glass pitcher and add:
Pour back and forth from one measure or pitcher into another measure or pitcher until the liquid is thoroughly mixed. Bottle and cork.

div.head: BRACE UP
div.p: 1 tablespoonful Bar Sugar in large Mixing glass.
Shake well; strain into tall, thin glass; fill with Apollinaris and serve.

div.head: BRANDY AND GINGER ALE
div.p: 3 lumps of Ice in tall, thin glass.

div.head: BRANDY AND SODA
div.p: 2 pieces of Ice in tall, thin glass.

div.head: BRANDY FLIP
div.p: Fill medium. Bar glass ¼ full Shaved Ice.
Shake well; strain into small Shell glass; grate a little Nutmeg on top and serve.

div.head: BRANDY FLOAT
div.p: Fill a Cocktail glass ⅔ full of Carbonated Water.

div.head: BRANDY JULEP
div.p: Into a small Bar glass pour ¾ Wineglass of Water and stir in 1 heaping teaspoonful of Bar Sugar. Bruise 3 or 4 sprigs of Mint in the Sugar and Water with a Muddler until the flavor of the Mint has been extracted. Then withdraw the Mint and pour the flavored Water into a tall Shell glass or large Goblet, which has been filled with fine Ice, and add:
Stir well; decorate with few sprigs of Mint by planting the sprigs stems downward in the Ice around the rim of glass; dress with Fruit and serve.

div.head: BRANDY PUNCH
div.p: Fill large Bar glass ¾ full Shaved Ice.
2 teaspoonfuls Bar Sugar dissolved in little Water.
Shake; dress with Fruit and serve with Straw.

div.head: BRANDY SCAFFA
div.p: In equal proportion to fill the glass, using care as in preparing Crustas, not to allow the colors to blend.

div.head: BRANDY SHAKE
div.p: Fill small Bar glass ¾ full Shaved Ice.
Shake; strain into small fancy glass and serve.

div.head: BRANDY SHRUB (2-gallon mixture for 40 people)
div.p: Into a Punch bowl put the Peeled Rinds of 5 Lemons and the Juice of 12 Lemons and add 5 quarts of Brandy. Make the bowl airtight and set it aside. At the expiration of 6 days add 3 quarts of Sherry wine and 6 pounds of Loaf Sugar, which has been dissolved in 1 quart of plain Soda. Strain through a bag and bottle.

div.head: BRANDY SKIN
div.p: Fill a Whiskey glass ½ full Hot Water and pour in:
Twist a piece of Lemon Skin on top and serve.
(It may occur that a customer will ask for a little Sugar. In that case add ½ small teaspoonful, and stir).

div.head: BRANDY SLING
div.p: 1 teaspoonful Sugar dissolved in little Water.
Stir; twist in a piece of Lemon Peel; grate Nutmeg on top and serve.

div.head: BRANDY SMASH
div.p: Fill large Bar glass ½ full Shaved Ice.
Stir; strain into fancy Stem glass and serve.

div.head: BRANDY SOUR
div.p: Fill large Bar glass ¾ full Shaved Ice.
Stir; strain into Sour glass; dress with Fruit and serve.

div.head: BRANDY TODDY
div.p: Into a Whiskey glass drop 1 lump Cracked Ice.
1 teaspoonful of Bar Sugar dissolved in little Water.
Stir; place the bottle before the customer and allow him to pour his own drink.

div.head: BRONX COCKTAIL
div.p: Fill large Bar glass ¾ full Shaved Ice.
Shake well; strain into Cocktail glass and serve.

div.head: BURNT BRANDY
div.p: Place two lumps of Cut Loaf Sugar in a small, shallow dish or saucer and pour over the Sugar 1½ jiggers of Cognac Brandy. Ignite the Sugar and Brandy and let them burn for about two minutes. Then cover the dish or saucer with a plate, and when the fire is extinguished pour the liquid into a small Bar glass and serve.

div.head: BUSTER BROWN COCKTAIL
div.p: Fill large Bar glass ⅔ full Shaved Ice.
Stir; strain into Cocktail glass and serve.

div.head: BUTTERED RUM
div.p: In a Tumbler drop 1 lump of Sugar and dissolve it in a little hot Water, and add:
1 piece of Butter about the size of a Walnut.
Grate Nutmeg on top and serve.

div.head: CALIFORNIA SHERRY COBBLER
div.p: 1 pony of Pineapple Syrup in large Bar glass.
Fill glass with Shaved Ice; stir well; decorate with Fruit; dash a little Port Wine on top and serve with Straws.

div.head: CALIFORNIA WINE COBBLER
div.p: Fill tall, thin glass nearly full Shaved Ice.
Stir; ornament with Fruit and serve with Straws.

div.head: CARLETON RICKEY—St. Louis Style
div.p: Use a large Mixing glass; fill with lump Ice.

div.head: CATAWBA COBBLER
div.p: Fill large Bar glass ½ full of Shaved Ice.
1 teaspoonful Bar Sugar dissolved in a little Water.
Fill with Shaved Ice; stir well; decorate with Berries and serve with Straws.

div.head: CELERY SOUR
div.p: Fill large Bar glass full Shaved Ice.
Stir; strain into Fancy Wineglass with Fruit and serve.

div.head: CENTURY CLUB PUNCH (for a party of 5)
div.p: Fill glass Pitcher ¼ full Cracked Ice.
Stir well and serve in Punch glasses.

div.head: CHAMPAGNE
div.p: Serve off the Ice very cold. Ice should never be put in the Wine.

div.head: CHAMPAGNE COBBLER
div.p: 1 teaspoonful Bar Sugar in large Bar glass.
Fill glass ½ full Shaved Ice and fill up with Champagne. Decorate with Fruit and serve with Straws.

div.head: CHAMPAGNE COCKTAIL
div.p: 1 lump Sugar in tall, thin glass.

div.head: CHAMPAGNE CUP (2-gallon mixture)
div.p: For mixing use a large Punch bowl or other suitable vessel of glass or porcelain lined.
Stir well and allow mixture to stand three hours. Strain into another bowl and add:
Stir well; decorate with Fruit; float slices of Grape Fruit on top and serve in Champagne glasses.

div.head: CHAMPAGNE FRAPPE
div.p: Place a bottle in a Champagne cooler and around it a freezing mixture of fine Ice and Salt. Twirl the bottle until it is about to freeze, when it will be ready to serve.

div.head: CHAMPAGNE JULEP
div.p: Fill medium size Shell glass ⅓ full Cracked Ice.
Pour Champagne slowly into the glass, stirring gently at the same time.
Dress with fruit; dash with Brandy and serve with Straws.

div.head: CHAMPAGNE PUNCH (for a party of 6)
div.p: Into a glass Pitcher pour the Juice of 1 Lemon, and add:
Stir with Ladle and drop in:
Decorate with Fruit and serve in Champagne goblets.

div.head: CHAMPAGNE SOUR
div.p: Fill medium Bar glass ⅓ full Shaved Ice.
Stir gently; dress with Fruit and Berries; dash with Brandy and serve with Straws.

div.head: CHAMPAGNE VELVET
div.p: Fill Goblet ½ full ice-cold Champagne. Fill up balance of Goblet with ice-cold Porter. Stir and serve.

div.head: CHOCOLATE PUNCH
div.p: Fill large Bar glass ⅔ full Shaved Ice.
Fill up with Milk; shake well; strain into Punch glass; grate Nutmeg on top and serve.

div.head: CIDER EGGNOG
div.p: Into a large Bar glass break a fresh Egg.
Shake; strain into tall, thin glass and serve with grated Nutmeg on top.

div.head: CLARET AND ICE
div.p: 4 lumps Ice in medium size Mineral Water glass.
Fill up with Claret and serve.

div.head: CLARET COBBLER
div.p: Dissolve one teaspoonful of Sugar with little Water in large Bar glass.
Fill up with Shaved Ice and serve with Straws.

div.head: CLARET CUP (2-gallon mixture)
div.p: For mixing use a large Punch bowl or other suitable vessel of glass or porcelain lined.

Mix well with a Ladle and set aside for three hours before using. Then strain info another bowl, and when ready to use add 3 pints of some sparkling Wine, preferably Champagne. Stir gently once or twice, and then put in a block of clear Ice and decorate the top of it tastily with Fruits and let several slices of Grape Fruit float around in the bowl. Serve in Champagne glasses.

div.head: CLARET FLIP
div.p: Fill large Bar glass ½ full Shaved Ice.
2 heaping teaspoonfuls Bar Sugar dissolved in a little Water.
Shake thoroughly; strain into Punch glass; sprinkle with Nutmeg on top and serve.

div.head: CLARET PUNCH
div.p: Fill large Bar glass ⅔ full Shaved Ice.
Shake; strain into thin glass; dress with Fruit and serve with Straws.

div.head: CLARET PUNCH (5-gallon mixture for a large reception or party of 100 people)
div.p: For mixing use a large agate or porcelain-lined vessel.
Place a large block of Ice in a Punch bowl and fill nearly full of the mixture, adding:
Serve from the bowl into Punch glasses with a Ladle, and renew the contents of the bowl from the mixing vessel as needed.

div.head: CLOVER CLUB COCKTAIL
div.p: Fill large Bar glass ½ full Fine Ice.
Shake well; strain into Cocktail glass and serve.

div.head: CLOVER LEAF COCKTAIL
div.p: Fill Mixing glass with Lump Ice.
1 jigger Sir Robert Burnette's Old Tom Gin.
Shake well and strain into a Cocktail glass.

div.head: CLUB COCKTAIL
div.p: Fill large Bar glass ½ full Shaved Ice.
Stir; strain into Cocktail glass; dress with Berries; dash with Champagne; twist a piece of Lemon Skin over the drink and drop it on top. Serve.

div.head: CLUB HOUSE CLARET PUNCH
div.p: Fill large Bar glass ¾ full Shaved Ice.
Shake; strain into tall, thin glass; fill up with Apollinaris or Seltzer; dress with Fruit and serve.

div.head: CLUB HOUSE PUNCH (for a party of 20)
div.p: For mixing use a large Punch bowl.

Set this mixture aside in ice box for 6 hours. Then place block of Ice in another bowl of sufficient capacity and strain in the mixture from the Mixing bowl. Dress the Ice with Fruit and serve with a Ladle into Punch glasses.

div.head: COFFEE COCKTAIL
div.p: Fill large Bar glass ⅔ full Shaved Ice.
Shake; strain into medium thin glass; grate Nutmeg on top and serve.

div.head: COHASSET PUNCH
div.p: Fill large Bar glass ½ full Shaved Ice.
Stir and serve with a Preserved Peach and its liquor.

div.head: COLD RUBY PUNCH (2½-gallon mixture for 50 people)
div.p: (See instructions for mixing and serving Punches in quantities.)

div.head: COLUMBIA SKIN
div.p: This drink is identical with Whiskey Skin.
COMPANION PUNCH (2½-gallon mixture for a reception or party of 50 people)
Into a large Punch bowl pour:
6 quarts equal parts Sweet and Dry Catawba.
When well stirred place large block of Ice in center of bowl; dress the Ice with Fruit and serve with a Ladle into Punch glasses.

div.head: CONTINENTAL SOUR
div.p: Fill a large Bar glass ⅔ full Shaved Ice.
1 teaspoonful Bar Sugar dissolved in little Water.
1 jigger of Whiskey, Brandy or Gin, as preferred.
Shake; strain into Sour glass; dash with Claret and serve.

div.head: CORDIAL LEMONADE
div.p: Add to a plain Lemonade ⅓ Jigger of any Cordial which the customer may prefer, and serve.

div.head: COUNTRY COCKTAIL
div.p: Fill large Bar glass ⅔ full Shaved Ice.
Shake well; strain into thin glass; grate Nutmeg on top and serve.

div.head: COUPEREE
div.p: Fill large Bar glass ⅓ full Ice Cream.
Fill up with Plain Soda; grate Nutmeg on top and serve.

div.head: CREME DE MENTHE
div.p: Fill a Sherry glass with Shaved Ice.
Cut Straw in two pieces and serve.

div.head: CRIMEAN CUP A LA MARMORA (for a party of 10)
div.p: Into a small Punch bowl pour:
Stir well; pack the bowl in Fine Ice, and when cold serve in fancy Stem glasses.

div.head: COUNTRY CLUB PUNCH
div.p: Take 1½ lbs. of Cut Loaf Sugar and rub the lumps on the skins of 4 Lemons and 2 Oranges until the Sugar becomes well saturated with the oil from the skins. Then put the Sugar thus prepared into a large porcelain-lined or agate Mixing vessel, and add:
Stir thoroughly with oak paddle or large silver ladle, and add:
4 quarts Tokay or Sweet Catawba Wine.

Mix well with oak paddle or ladle and strain into another bowl in which has been placed a block of clear ice. Then pour in 6 quarts Champagne. Decorate the Ice with Fruits, Berries, etc. Serve in Punch cups or glasses, dressing each glass with Fruit and Berries from the bowl.

div.head: COOPERSTOWN COCKTAIL
div.p: One jigger of Sir Robert Burnette's Old Tom Gin.
Strain and serve in Cocktail glass.

div.head: CURACOA
div.p: Into a bottle which will hold a full quart, or a little over, drop 6 ounces of Orange Peel sliced very thin, and add 1 pint of Whiskey. Cork the bottle securely and let it stand two weeks, shaking the bottle frequently during that time. Next strain, the mixture, add the Syrup, pour the strained mixture back into the cleaned bottle and let it stand 3 days, shaking well now and then during the first day. Next, pour a teacupful of the mixture into a mortar and beat up with it 1 drachm Powdered Alum, 1 drachm Carbonate of Potash. Put this mixture back into the bottle and let it stand for 10 days, at the expiration of which time the Curacoa will be clear and ready for use.

div.head: CURACOA PUNCH
div.p: Fill large Bar glass ¾ full Shaved Ice.
Stir; decorate with Fruit and Serve with Straws.

div.head: CURRANT SHRUB
div.p: For mixing use a porcelain-lined or agate vessel, and put in:

Place vessel on the fire and let it boil slowly for 10 minutes, and skim well while boiling. Then remove vessel from fire and add ½ gill of Brandy to every pint of Shrub. Bottle and cork securely. This drink is served by simply pouring a little of the Syrup into Ice Water, as any drink from Fruit Syrup is prepared. The basis preparation for all Shrubs or Small Fruits, such as Cherries, Raspberries, etc., is prepared in the same way as directed for Currant Shrub, varying the quantity of Sugar used to suit the kind of Fruit.

div.head: DERONDA COCKTAIL
div.p: Fill large Bar glass with Shaved Ice.
Shake; strain into Cocktail glass and serve.

div.head: DIARRHEA DRAUGHT
div.p: Grate Nutmeg on top and serve.

div.head: DIXIE COCKTAIL
div.p: Add to a plain Whiskey Cocktail:

div.head: DREAM
div.p: Fill large Bar glass ⅔ full Shaved Ice.
Shake thoroughly; strain into tall, thin glass; cover the top lightly with Creme de Menthe and serve.

div.head: DELUSION
div.p: Use a large Mixing glass; fill with Shaved Ice.
Shake well; strain into thin Stem glass and serve.

div.head: DORAY PUNCH
div.p: Fill large Bar glass ⅔ full Shaved Ice.
Shake hard; strain into thin Bar glass; dress with Fruit; dash with Seltzer; grate Nutmeg on top and serve.

div.head: DORAY SOUR
div.p: Fill large Bar glass ⅔ full Shaved Ice.
½ jigger Tokay or Sweet Catawba Wine.
Stir well and strain into a fancy Sour glass; dress with Fruits; dash with Apollinaris or Seltzer; top off with a little Claret and serve.

div.head: DUPLEX COCKTAIL
div.p: Fill large Bar glass with Shaved Ice.
Shake; strain into Cocktail glass and serve.

div.head: DURKEE COCKTAIL
div.p: Fill large Bar glass ⅔ Full Shaved Ice.
Shake well; strain into tall, thin glass; fill up with Plain Soda; stir gently and serve.

div.head: EAGLE PUNCH
div.p: Into a Hot Water glass drop:
1 lump Cut Loaf Sugar and dissolve in little Hot Water, crashing with muddler.
Fill up with boiling Water; twist a piece of Lemon Peel and grate Nutmeg on top and serve.

div.head: EAST INDIA COCKTAIL
div.p: Fill large Bar glass ¾ full Shaved Ice.
Stir well; strain into Cocktail glass and serve with a piece of twisted Lemon Peel on top.

div.head: EGG MILK PUNCH
div.p: Fill large Bar glass ½ full Shaved Ice.
Fill up with Milk; shake thoroughly until the mixture creams; strain into tall thin glass; grate Nutmeg on top and serve.

div.head: EGGNOG
div.p: Fill large Bar glass ½ full Shaved Ice.
Fill up with Milk; shake thoroughly; strain into tall, thin glass and serve with little Nutmeg grated on top.

div.head: EGGNOG (bowl of 3 gallons)
div.p: Beat the yolks of 20 Eggs until thin and stir in 2½ lbs. Bar Sugar until Sugar is thoroughly dissolved. Into this mixture pour:

Mix the ingredients well by stirring. Then pour in the milk slowly, stirring all the while to prevent curdling. Pour carefully over the top of the mixture the whites of the Eggs, which have been beaten to a stiff froth. Fill Punch glasses from the bowl with ladle and sprinkle a little Nutmeg over each glassful.

div.head: EGG SOUR
div.p: Shake well; grate Nutmeg on top and serve with Straw.

div.head: EL DORADO PUNCH
div.p: Fill large Bar glass nearly full Shaved Ice.
Shake; dress with Fruit and serve with Straws.

div.head: ENGLISH BISHOP PUNCH
div.p: Roast an Orange before a fire or in a hot oven. When brown cut it in quarters and drop the pieces, with a few Cloves, into a small porcelain-lined or agate vessel, and pour in 1 quart of hot Port Wine. Add 6 lumps Cut Loaf Sugar and let the mixture simmer over the fire for 30 minutes. Serve in Stem glasses with Nutmeg grated on top.

div.head: FANCY WHISKEY SMASH
div.p: Fill large Bar glass ½ full Shaved Ice.
3 sprigs Mint pressed with muddler in 1 jigger aerated Water.
Stir well; strain into Sour glass; dress with Fruit and serve.

div.head: FANNIE WARD
div.p: Use a large Mixing glass with Lump Ice.
Shake and strain into Cocktail glass.

div.head: FEDORA
div.p: Fill large Bar glass ¾ full Shaved Ice.
2 teaspoonfuls Bar Sugar dissolved in little Water.
Shake well; dress with Fruit and serve with Straws.

div.head: FISH CLUB PUNCH (for a party of 8)
div.p: Stir well; ladle into Punch glass and serve.

div.head: FOG HORN—Country Club Style
div.p: Use a large Mixing glass; fill with Lump Ice.
Stir well; strain into tall, thin glass and fill with imported Ginger Ale.

div.head: FREE LOVE COCKTAIL—-Club Style
div.p: ½ of the white of 1 Egg.
Shake well, serve in Cocktail glass.

div.head: FRENCH POUSSE CAFE
div.p: Fill a Pousse Cafe glass ½ full of Maraschino and add: Raspberry Syrup, Vanilla, Curacoa, Chartreuse and Brandy in equal proportions until the glass is filled. Then proceed as for Abricontine Pousse Cafe.

div.head: GARDEN PUNCH (2½ gallon mixture for a party of 50)
div.p: Place a good size block of Ice in a large Punch bowl.
6 Quarts Tokay or Sweet Catawba Wine.
Stir well; ladle into Stem glasses, and decorate each glass with Fruit before serving.

div.head: G.O.P.
div.p: Use a large Mixing glass with Lump of Ice.
Stir; ornament with Fruit and serve with Straws.

div.head: GIBSON COCKTAIL
div.p: Use a large Mixing glass with Lump Ice.
Stir; strain and serve in Cocktail glass.

div.head: GILLETTE COCKTAIL—Chicago Style
div.p: Use a large Mixing glass; fill with Lump Ice.
Stir well and strain into Cocktail glass.

div.head: GIN AND CALAMUS
div.p: Put ½ oz. of Calamus Root, which has been steeped, into a quart bottle of Gin.
Serve as you would a Straight Drink.

div.head: GIN DAISY
div.p: Juice of ½ of a Lime.
1 jigger Sir Robert Burnette's Old Tom Gin.
Serve in a Mug with Lump Ice; fill with Seltzer.
Stir well and decorate with the skin of the Lime and fresh Mint and serve with Straws.

div.head: GIN SOUR—Country Club Style
div.p: Shake well; strain into Cocktail glass and serve.

div.head: GIN SQUASH—Country Club Style
div.p: Use a large glass Stein; fill with Lump Ice.
Fill with Seltzer: stir well and serve.

div.head: GOLFER'S DELIGHT—Home of Bevo—18th Hole.
div.p: Use a large glass Pitcher; fill with Lump Ice.
Stir well and serve in a Beer glass.

div.head: HORSE THIEF COCKTAIL
div.p: Fill a large Mixing glass with Lump Ice.
1 jigger Sir Robert Burnette's Old Tom Gin.
Stir well and serve in a Cocktail glass.

div.head: IRISH ROSE—Country Club Style
div.p: Use a tall, thin glass; fill with Cracked Ice.

div.head: JERSEY LIGHTNING COCKTAIL
div.p: Use large Mixing glass; fill with Lump Ice.
Stir well; strain and serve in Cocktail glass.

div.head: KNABENSCHUE—Country Club Style
div.p: Use a small stone Mug; Lump Ice.
Stir well; dress with fresh Mint and serve.

div.head: L.P.W.
div.p: 1 jigger of Sir Robert Burnette's Old Tom Gin.
Stir well and strain into a Cocktail glass.
Add a Pickeled Onion and serve.

div.head: LADIES' DELIGHT—Thursday Luncheon Punch
div.p: 1 quart of Old Country Club Brandy.
Use a large Punch bowl with one Lump of Ice.
Pour in mixture; add one quart of Cook's Imperial Champagne.
Stir well; decorate with fresh Mint, Fruit in season, and serve.

div.head: LEAPING FROG
div.p: Shake well and strain into Stem glass.

div.head: LEMONADE APOLLINARIS (or Carbonated Water)
div.p: Fill large Mixing glass ⅔ full fine Ice.
Fill up with Apollinaris or suitable Carbonated Water. Stir; strain into Lemonade glass; dress with Fruit and serve.

div.head: LONE TREE COCKTAIL
div.p: Use a large Mixing glass; fill with Lump Ice.
Shake well; serve in Cocktail glass.

div.head: MINT JULEP—Kentucky Style
div.p: Dissolve one lump of Sugar in one-half pony of Water.
Two jiggers of Old Bourbon Whiskey.
Stir well; add one boquet of Mint and serve.
Be careful and not bruise the Mint.

div.head: OVERALL JULEP—St. Louis Style
div.p: Use a large Mixing glass; fill with Lump Ice.
Shake well; pour into tall, thin glass; add one bottle Imported Club Soda and serve.

div.head: ONION COCKTAIL
div.p: ½ of Italian Vermouth and no Bitters used.
Large Bar glass with Cracked Ice and stir well.
Strain and serve with an Onion.

div.head: OLD FASHION COCKTAIL
div.p: 1 lump of Sugar and dissolve in Water.
Twist piece of Lemon Skin over the drink and drop it in. Stir well and serve.

div.head: OJEN COCKTAIL
div.p: Juice of ½ of a Lime.

div.head: PEQUOT SEMER
div.p: Use a tall, thin Bar glass.
1 jigger of Sir Robert Burnette's Old Tom Gin.
Crush ingredients together; fill with Lump Ice; add Seltzer. Stir well and serve.

div.head: PINEAPPLE JULEP (for a party of 6—Use a small punch bowl)
div.p: 1 jigger Sir Robert Burnette's Old Tom Gin.
Place large square of Ice in bowl; dress with the Fruits and serve Julep in fancy Stem glass.

div.head: POLO PLAYERS' DELIGHT—Horse's Neck
div.p: 1 jigger Sir Robert Burnette's Old Tom Gin.

div.head: POUSSE CAFE—St. Louis
div.p: Pour in Pousse Cafe glass as follows:
In preparing the above use a small Wineglass with spoon for pouring in each Cordial separately.
Be careful they do not mix together.

div.head: PUNCH A LA ROMAINE (for a party of 16)
div.p: 2 tablespoons Dr. Siegert's genuine Angostura Bitters.
Dissolve the Sugar in the Juice of the Lemons and Oranges adding the Rind of 1 Orange.
Strain through a Sieve into a bowl and add by degrees the whites of the Eggs beaten to a froth.
Place the bowl on Ice till cold, then stir in the Rum and Wine until thoroughly mixed. Serve in fancy Stem glasses.

div.head: RAMOS GIN FIZZ—Country Club Style
div.p: Shake well; strain into Highball glass and serve.

div.head: REMSEN COOLER
div.p: Use a medium size Fizz glass.
Peel a Lemon as you would an Apple.
Place the Rind or Peeling into the Fizz glass.
Fill up the balance with Club Soda; stir up slowly with a spoon and serve.
In this country it is often the ease that people call a Remsen Cooler where they want Old Tom Gin or Sloe Gin instead of Scotch Whiskey. It is therefore the bartender's duty to mix as desired.

div.head: SEPTEMBER MORN COCKTAIL—Country Club Style
div.p: Use a large Mixing glass; fill with Lump Ice.
Shake well; strain into Cocktail glass and serve.

div.head: SHANDY GAFF
div.p: Fill half the glass with Porter and half with Ginger Ale. It is also made with half Ale and half Ginger Ale.

div.head: SHERRY AND BITTERS
div.p: Put 2 dashes Dr. Siegert's genuine Angostura Bitters in a Sherry glass and roil the glass 'till the Bitters entirely cover the inside surface.
Fill the glass with Sherry and serve.

div.head: STINGER—Country Club Style
div.p: Use a large Mixing glass; fill with Lump Ice.
Shake well; strain into Cocktail glass and serve.

div.head: STONE SOUR
div.p: Use a tall, thin glass; fill with fine Ice.
Leave in Ice; stir well and serve.

div.head: SAMTON COCKTAIL
div.p: Use a large Mixing glass with Cracked Ice.
Shake well; strain into Cocktail glass and serve.

div.head: TOM TOM
div.p: Use a large Brandy Roller glass.
Fill Roller half full of Fine Ice.
1 jigger of green Creme de Menthe and serve.

div.head: TOM AND JERRY
div.p: Make a batter by separating the yolks from whites of a given number of Eggs; beating the whites to a stiff froth and stirring the yolks until very thin. Then mix together in a Tom and Jerry bowl, stirring in Bar Sugar slowly until the batter is stiff and serve as follows:
Fill Tom and Jerry Mug ¼ full of Batter.
Stir well with Bar spoon; fill up with Hot Water; stir more; grate Nutmeg on top and serve.

div.head: TOKAY PUNCH
div.p: Out of 6 pounds of Tokay Grapes, select one pound to be put into the Punch last. Now make a boiling Syrup of three pounds of Sugar and one quart of boiling Water and pour this over the remaining five pounds of Grapes. When partly cold rub it through a sieve, leaving skins and seeds behind. Then add the Juice of two Oranges and two Lemons and one quart of St. Julien Claret, 1 jigger of Angostura Bitters.
Before serving add 1 pint of good Brandy and an Italian Meringue Paste of six Egg whites, colored a nice red and drop in the remaining Grapes.

div.head: TWILIGHT COCKTAIL
div.p: Use a large Mixing glass with Lump Ice.
Shake well; strain into a Champagne glass; fill with Seltzer and serve.

div.head: WHISKEY PUNCH—St. Louis Style
div.p: Use a large Mixing glass; fill with Lump Ice.
Shake well; strain into Stem glass and serve.

div.head: WHISKEY SCOTCH HOT
div.p: 1 lump Sugar dissolved in Hot Whiskey glass.
Stir and serve with Nutmeg sprinkled on top.

div.head: WHISKEY IRISH HOT
div.p: Substitute Irish for Scotch Whiskey and proceed as for Hot Scotch Whiskey.

div.head: INDEX
div.p: Claret Punch (5-gallon mixture for a large reception or party of 100 people)
Cold Ruby Punch (2½-gallon mixture for 50 people)
Companion Punch (2½-gallon mixture for a reception or party of 50 people)
